description: We are a team of developers, researchers, problem-solvers, and space enthusiasts. We aim to create a practical, intuitive, and reliable solution for monitoring health indicators and supporting informed decisions. We welcome teammates with skills or interests in AI/ML, software development, data science, biomedical systems, UI/UX, visualization, cloud, and system design.
summary:
Our application is a prototype health-monitoring dashboard designed to assist astronauts during long-duration space missions. It integrates vital signs, health trends, physiological signal visualizations, and medical history into a unified interface, enabling crew members to monitor and review their health changes over time.

The backend processes EEG, respiratory, and galvanic skin response (GSR) signals at five-second intervals, extracts relevant features, and applies an autoencoder-based model to detect unusual patterns. Based on the detected deviations, it classifies health status into three levels: Stable, Monitor, and Elevated Deviation.

The main objective is to encourage astronauts to take an active role in monitoring their health, particularly in environments where immediate medical support from Earth may be limited. By presenting health indicators and physiological changes in an intuitive and accessible format, the dashboard aims to facilitate early recognition of potential abnormalities and indicate when further attention may be required. As spaceflight can affect both physical and behavioral health, continuous monitoring is essential for supporting crew wellbeing. However, the current prototype uses sample data, and practical deployment would require validated sensors, extensive testing, and appropriate clinical supervision.
details:
Project overview

Our application is a prototype dashboard designed to help astronauts review their health information during long-duration space missions. It presents vital sign summaries, overall health trends, physiological signal visualizations, and medical history in one interface. The aim is to make health information easier to understand and help crew members identify changes that may require further attention.

How it works

The analysis prototype operates on five-second signal windows sampled at 256 Hz. A Python-based feature extraction pipeline computes 35 selected features from EEG, respiratory (“R”), and galvanic skin response (GSR) signals. A FastAPI service processes the scaled feature vector using an ONNX-based autoencoder to generate an anomaly score and assign one of three health status levels: Stable, Monitor, or Elevated Deviation.

Currently, the dashboard operates using sample data, while the analysis endpoint receives extracted features rather than connecting directly to wearable sensors. These status labels are intended to serve as indicators for further review, not as medical diagnoses.

Benefits and intended impact

By presenting health indicators and trends together, the application aims to encourage astronauts to monitor their own health and recognize changes that may require closer observation or professional attention. It is particularly intended to support crew awareness in situations where immediate medical assistance from Earth may be unavailable.

Tools and technology

The dashboard was developed using JavaScript, React, and CSS. The analysis prototype uses Python, PyTorch, and ONNX inference. At present, the system does not integrate live medical sensors. Future implementation may involve validated wearable devices for EEG, respiratory, and GSR monitoring.

Creativity and design considerations

The project brings together a crew-oriented health review interface and a physiological signal-analysis prototype, going beyond simply displaying model outputs. Design considerations include the challenges of long-duration missions, the clarity of health trend interpretation, the potential for false alarms, and the importance of avoiding misleading interpretations of anomaly scores. Practical implementation would require sensor integration, testing with appropriate datasets, privacy safeguards, and proper clinical and mission-specific supervision.
dataRefs: Flight Crew Physiological Data for Crew State Monitoring
